Apple Unveils Its First Touchscreen MacBook Pro Featuring PROLED XDR Display

Apple Enters the Touchscreen Laptop Market

Apple has officially announced its first-ever full touchscreen MacBook Pro during the 'Pro and Tell' event in Cupertino. Dubbed the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, the new device breaks from the company's long-standing design philosophy regarding touch interfaces on laptops, bringing a Tandem OLED touch display to both 14-inch and 16-inch form factors.

The hardware announcement represents a major shift for Apple's professional laptop lineup, integrating touch capabilities alongside high-end internal components designed for creative professionals and power users.

Specifications and Performance

Under the hood, the new touchscreen MacBook Pro models are powered by Apple's M5 Pro and M5 Max processors, differing from the mainstream M6 chip configurations seen in standard updates.

Key hardware details confirmed in the announcement include:

  • Display: Tandem OLED touch display featuring up to 2,000 nits of brightness, with a color gamut supporting both P3 and Adobe RGB spectrums.
  • Processors: Configurable with M5 Pro (up to 15-core CPU and 16-core GPU) or M5 Max (up to 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU).
  • Memory and Storage: Configurations scale up to 128GB of RAM and up to a massive 16TB SSD option.

Pricing and Availability

Entry-level pricing for the new lineup begins at $2,899 for the 14-inch model, which includes an M5 Pro chip, 24GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. The 16-inch base model starts at $3,399 with a baseline M5 Pro configuration, 24GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. Fully maxed-out configurations featuring the M5 Max, 128GB of RAM, and a 16TB SSD reach up to $14,399.

Preorders are available immediately, with official store shelf availability scheduled for November 6.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

For consumers and professionals evaluating the new hardware, several factors are important to consider regarding what is confirmed versus what remains to be tested:

  • Confirmed Facts: Official pricing, base configurations, screen sizes (14 and 16 inches), processor options (M5 Pro and M5 Max), and release schedule (preorders live now, shipping November 6) are officially detailed by the manufacturer.
  • Historical Context: While historical company commentary famously resisted touchscreen laptops, Apple previously experimented with touch interfaces via the Touch Bar on late-2010s MacBook Pro models.
  • Unknowns: Real-world battery performance under heavy Tandem OLED touch usage, ergonomic comfort of prolonged vertical touch input on macOS, and independent benchmark testing remain to be seen once review units reach consumers.

Readers can verify these announcements and check further updates directly by visiting the original reporting at [IGN](https://www.ign.com/articles/apple-announces-its-first-touchscreen-macbook).
